technology_name: A METHOD FOR FABRICATING BIODEGRADABLE MAGNESIUM-BASED IMPLANTS USING A 3D-PRINTING PROCESS
institution: National Institute of Technology Calicut (NIT Calicut)
problem_solved: Traditional structural bone implants utilize non-degradable metallic components that require risky, expensive follow-up secondary extraction surgeries and introduce long-term localized tissue stress-shielding artifacts.
description: An advanced additive manufacturing process deploying layer-by-layer 3D-printing mechanics to cleanly shape customizable, highly porous magnesium-based skeletal implants, featuring variable structural scaffold architectures embedded with patient-specific antibiotic drug profiles.
applications: Custom orthopedic reconstructive implants, load-bearing bone fracture fixation cages, bio-absorbable internal surgical clips, and dental maxillofacial scaffolding.
secondary_sector: Advanced Materials & Chemical, Robotics, Automation & Drones, Infrastructure, Construction & Smart Cities, Biotechnology & Life Sciences
